observations: Photo 0 shows a blue truck cab on a bare chassis frame with rear wheels, parked next to a blue metal cabinet or generator housing.
Photo 1 shows two weathered shipping containers, one yellow-brown and heavily rusted and one grey-white, on unpaved ground with pipes nearby.
Photo 2 shows an aged white cab-over truck on a flatbed trailer under a shelter, with a red truck bearing a DAF grille visible in the background.
All three photos carry a 'POSTED ON JIJI MERCHANT MAGNATE' watermark.
The seller text names 'huzhak steel company ltd' and describes scrap dealers buying nationwide and dealing in all kinds of industrial items.

claims.evidence: Seller text only; no photos or documents prove nationwide buying operations.

claims.evidence: Seller text only; photos show a truck chassis, containers, and trucks but do not prove the range of industrial items dealt in.

risks.risk: It is unclear which item, if any, is for sale because the photos show a truck chassis, shipping containers, and trucks.
risks.proof: A single clear photo of the specific item being offered, with the seller confirming it is the item for sale.

risks.risk: The seller describes a scrap-buying service rather than offering goods for sale, so the buyer may not be able to purchase anything.
risks.proof: Seller confirmation in writing that the items in the photos are for sale and not a request to buy scrap.

risks.risk: Condition, completeness, and operability of the vehicles and containers cannot be assessed from the photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photos and a short video of each item showing rust, missing parts, engine condition, and container integrity.

proof_requests: Ask the seller which specific item in the photos is for sale and request clear photos of that item only.
Ask whether the listing is to sell scrap or to buy scrap from the public.
Request close-up photos of any identification plates, brand names, and condition details for the item being sold.
response.reason: The photos show several different industrial items and the seller's words describe a scrap-buying company rather than a specific item for sale, so the item cannot be identified.
